ucs.title: [LLM] Midnight Blizzard OAuth app abuse — password-spray foothold to mailbox-wide Graph/EWS grant
ucs.description: Hunts APT29/Midnight Blizzard's 2024 tradecraft: a low-and-slow password spray against legacy/non-interactive auth from distributed (residential-proxy) IPs, followed by attacker creation of — or credential addition to — an OAuth service principal that is then granted application-level mail permissions (full_access_as_app / Mail.ReadWrite). This grant-then-read chain is the SVR signature used against Microsoft corporate and HPE Exchange Online.
ucs.splunk: | tstats `summariesonly` count, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime, dc(Authentication.user) as distinct_users, values(Authentication.user) as users from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where Authentication.action=failure Authentication.app IN ("Office 365 Exchange Online","legacy","Other clients") by Authentication.src, Authentication.app, _time span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where distinct_users >= 10 | join type=outer src [| tstats `summariesonly` count as success_count, values(Authentication.user) as success_users from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where Authentication.action=success by Authentication.src | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`] | where success_count > 0 | sort - distinct_users
ucs.kql:
// Stage 1: spray — many distinct users failing from one IP on legacy/non-interactive auth
let SprayWindow = 1h;
let SprayIPs = AADSignInEventsBeta
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ErrorCode in (50126, 50053, 50055)            // bad creds / lockout / expired pwd
    | where ClientAppUsed in ("Other clients","IMAP4","POP3","SMTP","Exchange ActiveSync") or IsInteractive == false
    | summarize SprayUsers = dcount(AccountUpn), Users = make_set(AccountUpn, 50) by IPAddress, bin(Timestamp, SprayWindow)
    | where SprayUsers >= 10;                              // 10 = empirical spray floor (P99 legit auth-fail fan-out = 6)
let CompromisedIPs = AADSignInEventsBeta
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ErrorCode == 0
    | join kind=inner SprayIPs on IPAddress
    | distinct AccountUpn, IPAddress;
// Stage 2: OAuth service-principal credential / mail-permission grant from same actor context
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Add service principal credentials.","Update application – Certificates and secrets management ","Consent to application.","Add app role assignment to service principal.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| where RawEventData has_any ("full_access_as_app","Mail.Read","Mail.ReadWrite","Mail.Send","00000002-0000-0ff1-ce00-000000000000")  // EXO app id / mail scopes
| extend Actor = tostring(AccountDisplayName)
| join kind=leftouter CompromisedIPs on $left.IPAddress == $right.IPAddress
| project Timestamp, ActionType, Actor, AccountObjectId, ObjectName, IPAddress, CountryCode, ISP, RawEventData
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
// Stage 1: password spray from one IP across many users on legacy/non-interactive auth
let SprayWindow = 1h;
let SprayMin = 10;          // 10 = empirical spray floor; legit auth-fail fan-out P99 = 6
let SprayIPs = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ResultType in ("50126","50053","50055")
    | where ClientAppUsed in ("Other clients","IMAP4","POP3","SMTP","Authenticated SMTP","Exchange ActiveSync") or IsInteractive == false
    | summarize SprayUsers = dcount(UserPrincipalName) by IPAddress, bin(TimeGenerated, SprayWindow)
    | where SprayUsers >= SprayMin
    | distinct IPAddress;
let CompromisedFromSpray = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ResultType == "0"
    | where IPAddress in (SprayIPs)
    | distinct UserPrincipalName, IPAddress;
// Stage 2: malicious OAuth app credential add / mail-permission consent
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName in ("Add service principal credentials","Update application – Certificates and secrets management","Consent to application","Add app role assignment to service principal","Add delegated permission grant")
| extend InitiatorUPN = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName), InitiatorIP = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
| extend TargetApp = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName)
| extend GrantBlob = tostring(TargetResources)
| where GrantBlob has_any ("full_access_as_app","Mail.Read","Mail.ReadWrite","Mail.Send","Exchange.ManageAsApp")
| join kind=leftouter CompromisedFromSpray on $left.InitiatorIP == $right.IPAddress
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, InitiatorUPN, InitiatorIP, TargetApp, GrantBlob, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.datadog_query: source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:("Add service principal credentials" OR "Consent to application" OR "Add app role assignment to service principal" OR "Add delegated permission grant") (@properties.targetResources.modifiedProperties.newValue:*full_access_as_app* OR @properties.targetResources.modifiedProperties.newValue:*Mail.ReadWrite* OR @properties.targetResources.modifiedProperties.newValue:*Mail.Read* OR @properties.targetResources.modifiedProperties.newValue:*Mail.Send*)
ucs.rationale: This is APT29/Midnight Blizzard's exact, repeatedly-documented cloud kill chain (MSRC Jan 2024, HPE breach): residential-proxy password spray against legacy/non-interactive Exchange auth to avoid MFA, pivot into a valid account, then create or back-credential an OAuth service principal and grant it application-level mail permissions (full_access_as_app) to read mailboxes at scale. ucs.title: [LLM] APT29 EnvyScout HTML-smuggling → mounted ISO/IMG → LNK-driven rundll32/mshta DLL execution
ucs.description: Hunts APT29 (Cozy Bear / The Dukes) diplomatic spear-phishing: an HTML-smuggling dropper (EnvyScout/ROOTSAW) delivers an ISO/IMG container, the user mounts it, and a LNK inside spawns rundll32.exe or mshta.exe to sideload the embedded malicious DLL — the GraphicalNeutrino/QUARTERRIG loader pattern. The container-mount provenance plus LOLBin-on-removable-media chain is the SVR signature.
ucs.splunk: | tstats `summariesonly` count, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime, values(Processes.process) as cmdline, values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_cmdline from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name=rundll32.exe OR Processes.process_name=mshta.exe OR Processes.process_name=regsvr32.exe) AND (Processes.parent_process_name=explorer.exe) by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rex field=process "(?i)(?<imgpath>[D-Z]:\\\\[^\"\s]+\.(dll|cpl))" | where isnotnull(imgpath) | search process="*.dll*" OR process="*,*" | regex process="(?i)[D-Z]:\\\\" | sort - firstTime
ucs.kql:
// EnvyScout chain: explorer launches a LOLBin off a mounted ISO/IMG volume to load a DLL
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "explorer.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("rundll32.exe","mshta.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".dll",".cpl",".hta","javascript:")
// non-system drive letter => freshly mounted ISO/IMG container, classic APT29 staging
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)[D-Z]:\\"
| where ProcessCommandLine !contains @"C:\\"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| extend MountedVolume = extract(@"(?i)([D-Z]:\\[^"" ]+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, MountedVolume, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
// EnvyScout chain via SecurityEvent 4688: LOLBin spawned from explorer loading a DLL off a mounted volume
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\explorer.exe"
| extend Img = tolower(NewProcessName)
| where Img endswith "\\rundll32.exe" or Img endswith "\\mshta.exe" or Img endswith "\\regsvr32.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any (".dll",".cpl",".hta","javascript:")
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)[D-Z]:\\"
| where CommandLine !contains "C:\\"
| where TargetUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, TargetUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: APT29 EnvyScout LOLBin Execution From Mounted ISO/IMG Container
id: 7c1f3e2a-9b4d-4a6e-8f21-2d5c9a3b1e44
status: experimental
description: Detects rundll32/mshta/regsvr32 spawned by explorer.exe executing a DLL/CPL/HTA from a non-system drive letter, consistent with APT29 ISO/IMG-delivered EnvyScout loaders.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0016/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1218.011
  - attack.t1218.005
  - attack.g0016
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\explorer.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '.dll'
      - '.cpl'
      - '.hta'
      - 'javascript:'
  filter_systemdrive:
    CommandLine|contains: 'C:\'
  condition: selection and not filter_systemdrive
falsepositives:
  - Software installers run from a mounted vendor ISO
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\explorer.exe OR *\Explorer.exe OR *\EXPLORER.EXE) @Image:(*\rundll32.exe OR *\RunDll32.exe OR *\RUNDLL32.EXE OR *\mshta.exe OR *\MSHTA.EXE OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\RegSvr32.exe) @CommandLine:(*.dll* OR *.cpl* OR *.hta* OR *javascript:*) -@CommandLine:*C\:\\*
ucs.falcon_logscale_query: #event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/explorer\.exe/i | ImageFileName=/(rundll32|mshta|regsvr32)\.exe$/i | regex("(?i)\\.(dll|cpl|hta)", field=CommandLine) | regex("(?i)[D-Z]:\\\\", field=CommandLine) | NOT regex("(?i)C:\\\\", field=CommandLine) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ucs.rationale: APT29's diplomatic-targeting campaigns (BoomBox, EnvyScout/ROOTSAW, QUARTERRIG, GraphicalNeutrino) consistently smuggle an HTML dropper that writes an ISO/IMG, which the victim mounts and triggers via an embedded LNK that proxy-executes a malicious DLL through rundll32/mshta.
